arxiv-1901-05302.title: Development of a system to profile foot temperatures of the plantar and the periphery Thanks: This work was supported by the National Science Foundation grant RPHS-2016-DTM02. Thanks: Department of Electronic and Telecommunication Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, University of Moratuwa, 10400 Ka
arxiv-1901-05302.description: Abstract Foot temperature profiling is of utmost importance is mitigating the adverse effects due to foot complications especially due to diabetes. Contactless temperature monitoring methods could be used effectively in large scale for patient screening. Near-infrared thermography has proven to be convenient and accurate for temperature profiling.

arxiv-1906-05756.title: In-situ Raman gain between hyperfine ground states in a potassium magneto-optical trap
arxiv-1906-05756.creator: Graeme Harvie, Adam Butcher, Jon Goldwin
arxiv-1906-05756.description: Abstract We study optical gain in a gas of cold 39 K atoms. The gain is observed during operation of a conventional magneto-optical trap without the need for additional fields. Measurements of transmission spectra from a weak probe show that the gain is due to stimulated Raman scattering between hyperfine ground states.

arxiv-2109-01912.title: Quantum reference frames: derivation of perspective-dependent descriptions via a perspective-neutral structure
arxiv-2109-01912.creator: Viktor Zelezny
arxiv-2109-01912.description: Abstract In standard quantum mechanics, reference frames are treated as abstract entities. We can think of them as idealized, infinite-mass subsystems which decouple from the rest of the system. In nature, however, all reference frames are realized through finite-mass systems that are subject to the laws of quantum mechanics and must be included in the dynamical evolution.

arxiv-2306-17774.title: Future stability of expanding spatially homogeneous FLRW solutions of the spherically symmetric Einstein–massless Vlasov system with spatial topology ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3}
arxiv-2306-17774.creator: Martin Taylor
arxiv-2306-17774.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Martin Taylor. Spatially homogeneous FLRW solutions constitute an infinite dimensional family of explicit solutions of the Einstein–massless Vlasov system with vanishing cosmological constant. Each member expands towards the future at a decelerated rate. These solutions are shown to be nonlinearly future stable to compactly supported spherically symmetric perturbations, in the case that the spatial topology is that of ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} .

arxiv-2405-05863.title: A Touch of Quantum Field Theory
arxiv-2405-05863.creator: Werner Nahm
arxiv-2405-05863.description: Abstract 1991 Mathematics Subject Classification 01A99, 81T99 1. Introduction In Srinivasa Ramanujan’s work there are at least three overlaps with quantum field theory, namely his treatment of divergent sums (chapter 6 of his second notebook [ 6 ] ), the Rogers-Ramanujan functions (chapter 16 [ 7 ] ), and mock theta series (Lost Notebook [ 3 ] ).

arxiv-2412-11765.title: Superradiant Neutrino Lasers from Radioactive Condensates
arxiv-2412-11765.creator: B.J.P. Jones, J. A. Formaggio
arxiv-2412-11765.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by B.J.P. Jones, J. A. Formaggio. Superradiance emerges from collective spontaneous emission in optically pumped gases, and is characterized by photon emission enhancements of up to 1 4 ​ N 2 \frac{1}{4}N^{2} in an N N atom system. The gain mechanism derives from correlations developed within the decay medium rather than from stimulated emission as in lasing, so an analog of this process should be possible for fermionic final states.

arxiv-2508-07605.title: Coordinated Power Management on Heterogeneous Systems Thanks:
arxiv-2508-07605.creator: Zhong Zheng, Zhiling Lan, Xingfu Wu, Valerie E. Taylor, Michael E. Papka
arxiv-2508-07605.description: Abstract Performance prediction is essential for energy-efficient computing in heterogeneous computing systems that integrate CPUs and GPUs. However, traditional performance modeling methods often rely on exhaustive offline profiling, which becomes impractical due to the large setting space and the high cost of profiling large-scale applications. In this paper, we present OPEN, a framework consists of offline and online phases.

pmc-11622206.title: The Imbalance of Homeostasis in Neutrophil Extracellular Traps is Associated with Portal Vein Thrombosis in Patients with Decompensated Cirrhosis
pmc-11622206.creator: Ming Han, Yujia Liu, Ying Cao, Yue Zhang, Yonghong Yan, Shuwei Deng, Xiaoxue Yuan, Huichun Xing, Yuan Huang, Liuluan Zhu
pmc-11622206.description: Background and AimsPortal vein thrombosis (PVT) is a challenging complication in liver cirrhosis, with no currently available sensitive diagnostic markers. This study aimed to investigate the potential of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and Deoxyribonuclease (DNase) as diagnostic indicators for PVT in chronic hepatitis B (CHB)-related decompensated cirrhosis.

pmc-12752241.title: High frequency of antibiotic administration for COVID-19 patients in Syria and its associations with mortality and complications
pmc-12752241.creator: Michael John Albdewi, Edwin Stimpson, Ibrahem Hanafi
pmc-12752241.description: BackgroundSyria’s healthcare system was severely challenged by the COVID-19 pandemic due to resource scarcity and a shortage of healthcare personnel. In this context, antibiotics were frequently prescribed empirically because of limited diagnostic capacity, concerns about secondary bacterial infections, and delayed hospitalization, despite the limited evidence of bacterial co-infection among patients with COVID-19.

pmc-13651282.title: The effects of precision intervention based on user profile on the improvement of postpartum parenting behavior for rural‑to‑urban floating women: a study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13651282.creator: Yani Deng, Lu Liu, Ting Li, Lingling Huang, Qiyu Fang, Jiangtao Ouyang, Jia Li, Jiali Wu, Jing Chen, Xujuan Zheng
pmc-13651282.description: BackgroundRural-to-urban floating women often face great challenges in postpartum parenting, which negatively affects the well-being of these women and their infants. User profiles allow tailored support, making precision interventions possible. Consequently, a randomized controlled trial (RCT) protocol was designed to evaluate the effects of user profile–based precision intervention on improving postpartum parenting behaviors for rural-to-urban floating women.
